Compare Bayesian Cure Models and Recommend a Distribution

Source: R/model_comparison.R
compare_models.Rd

Ranks two or more models fitted with `fit_bayesian_cure_model` to the same data by their expected out-of-sample predictive accuracy and reports which distribution for the non-cured patients is preferred. Models whose predictive accuracy is practically the same as that of the best one are flagged as practical ties.

Usage

compare_models(..., criterion = c("loo", "waic"), tie_elpd = 4, tie_se = 2)

# S3 method for class 'bcm_comparison'
print(x, digits = 1, ...)

Arguments

...

Two or more objects of class `bcm_fit`, for example `compare_models(fit1, fit2, fit3)`, or a single list of them. Models are labelled with the argument or list names and, failing that, with their distribution.

criterion

Character string. "loo" (default) uses approximate leave-one-out cross-validation with Pareto smoothed importance sampling; "waic" uses the widely applicable information criterion.

tie_elpd

Numeric. A model whose ELPD is lower than that of the best model by less than this amount (default 4) is a practical tie.

tie_se

Numeric. A model that is not a practical tie is "clearly worse" when the ELPD difference is at least this many standard errors (default 2) and "probably worse" otherwise.

x

An object of class `bcm_comparison`.

digits

Number of decimal places shown in the report.

Value

An object of class `bcm_comparison`, whose print method shows the report. It is a list with elements:

  • comparison: a data frame with one row per model, ordered from best to worst, with the difference in ELPD with respect to the best model and its standard error, the ELPD, the effective number of parameters, the information criterion, the stacking weight, for "loo" the largest Pareto k value, and the verdict.

  • best_model: the name of the model with the highest ELPD.

  • practical_ties: the names of the models that are practical ties with the best one.

  • recommendation: the text of the recommendation.

  • criterion, tie_elpd, tie_se: the settings used.

  • n_obs: the number of observations.

  • estimates: the list of objects returned by the `loo` package for each model.

Details

Fitting is the slow step, so the comparison works on models that have already been fitted, and possibly saved with `saveRDS`: nothing is refitted.

The pointwise log-likelihood of every model is computed from its posterior draws: an observed event contributes the density of the non-cured patients weighted by the probability of not being cured, and a censored observation contributes the mixture of the cure probability and the survival function of the non-cured patients. The expected log pointwise predictive density (ELPD) is then estimated with the `loo` package (Vehtari, Gelman and Gabry, 2017). Stacking weights (Yao et al., 2018) give the weight of each model in the combination with the best predictive performance. With `criterion = "loo"`, Pareto k values above 0.7 flag models for which the approximation is unreliable.

Each model receives a verdict:

  • "best": the highest ELPD.

  • "practical tie": the ELPD difference with the best model is below `tie_elpd`. Differences of this size are small: the models make very similar predictions and choosing one or the other has little consequence (Sivula et al., 2020).

  • "probably worse": the difference is at least `tie_elpd` but smaller than `tie_se` standard errors, so it is not conclusive.

  • "clearly worse": the difference is at least `tie_elpd` and at least `tie_se` standard errors.

Any threshold is a convention. Among practical ties the choice should rest on other grounds, such as the pre-specified model or parsimony, and the conclusions should be checked to agree across the tied models.

References

Vehtari A, Gelman A, Gabry J (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27, 1413-1432.

Yao Y, Vehtari A, Simpson D, Gelman A (2018). Using stacking to average Bayesian predictive distributions. Bayesian Analysis, 13, 917-1007.

Sivula T, Magnusson M, Matamoros AA, Vehtari A (2020). Uncertainty in Bayesian leave-one-out cross-validation based model comparison. arXiv:2008.10296.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
sim_data <- simulate_weibull_cure_data(
  n_patients = 300, cure_fraction_ctrl = 0.15, cure_fraction_exp = 0.40,
  max_follow_up = 36, weibull_shape = 1.2, median_survival_ctrl = 12,
  time_ratio_exp = 1.25
)
fit1 <- fit_bayesian_cure_model(sim_data, dist = "weibull")
fit2 <- fit_bayesian_cure_model(sim_data, dist = "lognormal")
fit3 <- fit_bayesian_cure_model(sim_data, dist = "loglogistic")
comparison <- compare_models(fit1, fit2, fit3)
comparison
comparison$comparison
} # }
